title: Open E1 Reviewer on the iPad and sign in
summary: Open your E1's /reviewer/ address in Safari on the iPad, sign in with your company account, and add it to the Home Screen; the E1 Reviewer app, once released, signs in the same way.

title: Your profile and organization
summary: The avatar in the top bar shows who is signed in, the organizations you belong to, the terms and conditions, and Sign out; tap another organization to work in it.

training.topic: Profile and organizations on the iPad

title: Terms and conditions on the iPad
summary: After you sign in for the first time, E1 Reviewer shows the E1 Terms and License Agreement; you accept it once for E1 and E1 Reviewer, and Profile → Terms and conditions shows it at any time.

title: The dashboard
summary: Home and each project's Overview show a dashboard of cards; in a project, every 2D space (with pins), the documents, pinned 2D spaces, redlines and recent changes.

title: Customize a dashboard for you, the project or the organization
summary: Customize adds, removes, orders and sizes the cards and saves the dashboard for you, for everyone in the project, or for everyone in the organization.
roles: Everyone for Just me; a project administrator for Everyone in the project; an organization administrator for Everyone in the organization

title: The Progress card: E1's dashboards on the iPad
summary: The Progress card shows E1's dashboards marked Show in E1 Reviewer, the environment's on Home and the project's in a project. Tap one to see it read-only; tap a number or a group to list its items and open one.
roles: Everyone; a tile counts only what you may open

title: Projects as tiles you arrange
summary: Projects, where E1 Reviewer starts, shows the search field and your projects as tiles; touch and hold a tile to arrange them.

title: The explorer
summary: E1's tree on the iPad: every project, its sections, folders, 2D spaces, objects, documents and tasks; a tap opens, touch and hold for more.
roles: Everyone with a role in the project

title: A project's 2D spaces
summary: A project's 2D spaces are under Model Space in the explorer, as in E1; one finger moves a 2D space, two fingers zoom; pin the ones you use most.
roles: Everyone with a role in the project

title: An object or a connection: properties, attributes, history and chat
summary: Tap a symbol, a pipe, a signal or a cable on a 2D space to see its object: properties, every attribute, its history and its chat.
roles: Everyone with a role in the project; writing in the chat needs a role that may comment

title: Photos and voice notes
summary: Take a photo with the iPad's camera or record a voice note and add it to an object, a comment or a task; they are kept with the object's files in E1.
roles: Everyone with a role in the project that may edit the object (adding files)

title: Redline a 2D space
summary: Redline draws on a 2D space with a pen, a cloud, an arrow, text or a stamp; each mark says what it means and carries a note, goes into a review round, and is answered by the engineers in E1.
roles: Everyone with a role in the project that may comment; setting another person's status needs a role that may resolve comments

title: For me: your tasks and checklists
summary: The Inbox (the bell on the rail) lists the tasks and checklists assigned to you in every project; tick items, comment with photos and voice notes, mark a task done.
roles: Everyone; ticking needs the task to be yours or a role that may edit it

training.topic: Tasks and checklists on the iPad

title: Offline in a walk-down
summary: Without the connection, what was opened on the iPad stays readable, and redlines, comments, photos, voice notes and ticks wait to be sent.

title: Notifications on the iPad
summary: When someone mentions you, answers you, assigns you a task or asks you to review, the iPad shows it, with the number of unread notifications on the app's icon; a tap opens what it is about.

title: Search
summary: The search field at the top of Projects finds projects, 2D spaces, objects and connections by tag or name, and tasks.

title: Alex on the iPad
summary: Alex on the iPad is Ask: questions typed or spoken with the microphone, answered without changing anything.
roles: Everyone with a role in the project
